dedupe_keys.name: usgs usmin commodity deposit data releases for the united states tin cobalt lithium tungsten graphite and others

description: This series of USGS data releases describes the mineral regions, mines and deposits in the United States that hold enrichments of single critical commodities: tin (more than 120 sites, 2018), cobalt (more than 60 sites, 2018), tellurium (2019), lithium (about 20 sites above 15,000 t, 2019), germanium (the Apex mine, 2020), tungsten (about 100 sites, version 2.0 2020), niobium (11 sites, 2021) with tantalum and gallium companions, graphite (10 sites, 2022) and indium (Bingham, West Desert and Chino, 2022). The ScienceBase pages say each release uses a size cutoff, draws on published papers, State, Federal and industry reports, and gives location, deposit type, commodities, production and resources; authors include Nick Karl, Meredith Burger, Keith Long, Jeffrey Mauk and colleagues. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC0-1.0. Access is free of charge. Coverage is national, including Alaska. Caveats: older resource figures may not comply with current reporting standards such as NI 43-101, and inclusion does not imply a deposit is economic. For simulation the releases locate domestic sources of battery, alloy and electronics inputs for supply disruption scenarios and hazard exposure of mines. Related catalogue records include the USGS Critical mineral deposits of the United States, the USGS Mineral Resources Data System and the USMIN mine features from topographic maps.
